newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Enterprise Oil profits surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Enterprise Oil profits surge.

text.p: Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc reported a 59 percent surge in first-half profits on Thursday and announced an oil exploration alliance with Pennzoil Co in the Gulf of Mexico.
The company said profit after tax jumped to 73.8 million pounds ($114.8 million) from 46.5 million a year earlier, boosted by higher oil prices and record production.
Enterprise said an important factor in the results was the higher oil price but said although it was seeing even higher prices at present, it remained cautious on the outlook.
"We haven't rebased our whole thinking on $22 (per barrel) oil," Enterprise finance director Andrew Shilston told Reuters.
"In common with others, we think next year it will head back to a $15-$18 range," he said.

Oil prices are around post-Gulf War highs at present, partly as a result of tension between the U.S. and Iraq, and Shilston acknowledged that the Iraq situation made the outlook for oil prices even harder to judge than usual.
At the same time, the company said it would pay a minimum of $100 million to Pennzoil to contribute to exploration costs in a deal which covers 102 Pennzoil leases in the Gulf of Mexico.
The company said the deal, which will earn it half of Pennzoil's interest in any new find, was an excellent way to move into area.
Enterprise international exploration director Andrew Armour told Reuters the deal was "a classic win-win", benefiting both companies.

He said the move, under negotiation since February, meant a rebalancing of Enterprise Oil's exploration portfolio, increasing its presence in the Gulf, where good prospects and extensive infrastructure offer potentially quicker returns than more frontier-type areas.

"They (Pennzoil) recognise that we have a lot to bring, including money," Armour said, adding that it fitted with Pennzoil, which is seen as looking to expand internationally and to focus on development in the Gulf rather than exploration.

He said Enterprise would bring exploration skills. "The geological setting is one we are very familiar with," he said, citing similarities with what Enterprise does in the north Sea in such fields as Arbroath and Nelson.
Enterprise will open an office in Houston and will contribute a minimum of $100 million through to 1998 to the project, which will take up 25 percent of the company's annual exploration budget.

Enterprise said its direct oil and gas production in the first half rose by two percent to 204,802 barrels per day, and Shilston said the group was on track to meet its target of raising production to 300,000 barrels by 1999.
Analysts generally welcomed the Pennzoil move, but Enterprise shares fell back after an initial rise, trading six pence lower at 518-1/2 after touching 533.
Analyst Irene Himona of Strauss Turnbull, who rates the shares a "very strong hold" put the fall down to profit taking, noting that the results were at the top end of market forecasts.
Earnings per share in the first half jumped to 13.5 pence from 8.2 and the company held its interim dividend at 6.5 pence.
